summary: A cast-iron tower on a timber crib at the end of a Lake Huron breakwater, lit in 1885 to mark a harbour of refuge, now toured by boat.

access.note: Offshore; reached by Preservation Society boat tours, summer Saturdays.

evidence.quote: Sand Beach was selected in 1872 as the site for an artificial harbor

evidence.quote: the breakwater provided the only safe refuge on the western coast of Lake Huron between Tawas Bay and the St. Clair River, a distance of 115 miles.

Fresnel lens was removed in 1986 and placed on display at the Grice House Museum in Harbor Beach.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: 1875 is the breakwater pier light (frame tower); 1885 is the present cast-iron tower. The record's 1858 (USLHS 'established') is not supported by any source read; the breakwater began in 1873.

notes_for_editor: Most narrative rests on Lighthousefriends (secondary, copyrighted; paraphrased). Lighthouse Board reports for 1875-1886 are not in the corpus, so construction dates are not checked against the primary reports. Fog-signal figures: LHB 1895 and 1900 reports (fiscal years ending June 30); the 1895 volume page is scan 384, printed page not read. Today's characteristic conflicts (record Fl G 4s; Wikipedia Al WR 10s), so omitted. NRHP 83000850 (listed 1983 per record) not read; nomination not digitised. Roster conflicts: LF lists Thomas E. Radcliff as head keeper (undated), not in USLHS; LF gives J.G. Johnson, USLHS James G. Johnson. 1858 'established' in the record looks wrong. The Life-Saving Service had a separate Sand Beach station; not covered. 1927 Fraser rescue date comes from LF; the Bulletin text was not read, only its index entry. Checker 2026-10-27: roster completed with pre-1959 USLHS lines; people serving from 1959 on (head keepers and USCG crews) are left out of the JSON per the living-people rule. Bulletin 1935 'p. 26 of the PDF' not independently confirmed (printed page about 223). Fraser was second assistant in 1927; the index calls him keeper.
